name: Garcinia cambogia (hydroxycitric acid)
short: A liver-injury registry identified 22 cases, one fatal, from Garcinia cambogia alone or in combinations (mostly with green tea); pooled randomised trials found no significant change in liver enzymes.
text: Among 1418 patients enrolled in a drug-induced liver injury registry from 2004 to 2018, the investigators identified 22 cases, adjudicated with high confidence, of liver injury from Garcinia cambogia taken alone (5 cases) or combined with green tea (16) or ashwagandha (1), so most cases involved combination products; 91% were hospitalised, one patient died and one required a liver transplant. The abstract's background describes the role of Garcinia cambogia in liver injury as controversial; the study's title states that Garcinia cambogia, either alone or in combination with green tea, causes moderate to severe liver injury, and its conclusion is that the liver injury caused by Garcinia cambogia and by green tea is clinically indistinguishable. A separate case series described four women with acute liver failure while taking Garcinia cambogia extract for weight loss. In contrast, a meta-analysis of nine randomised trial publications with 444 participants found no significant overall effect on the liver enzymes ALT or AST or on fasting blood sugar or insulin compared with control groups; in subgroup analyses insulin rose in women and both insulin and fasting blood sugar rose in participants with a BMI of 30 or more, while insulin fell when the extract was given for more than 8 weeks. The evidence of serious liver harm therefore comes from case reports and case series rather than trials. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
